content.title: Reload and fresh fetch confirm the upgraded Pro plan
content.intent: Prove that after a successful dashboard upgrade, a new account read and a page reload both reflect the persisted `pro` plan rather than stale client state.
content.technique_notes: Applied State / flow to the post-upgrade sequence and Persistence / refresh to the reload proof. Applied Equivalence partitioning to keep the source-defined eligible partition (`free`→`pro`) and to defer the unspecified already-`pro` partition to gap-1. No covering array was needed because the use-case exposed no independent input dimensions to combine; the risk-judged interaction strength would otherwise be 3 because the flow changes paid-plan entitlement.
